definition: Nadir means the lowest point something reaches.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word nadir. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know nadir should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The actor calls that year his nadir: evicted in March, dropped by his agent in June, and dressed as a giant taco outside a mall by August.
A dip is far milder than a nadir — a brief sag that recovers on its own, nowhere near the absolute bottom.
A slump is milder than a nadir — a bad stretch that can drag on, while the nadir is the single lowest point of the whole arc.

Rock bottom is the everyday, spoken phrase for as low as things can go, and it carries a shrug or a groan. Nadir says the same thing from an observatory: it surveys a whole arc — a career, an era — and marks its single lowest point in formal, written English.

A low point is the plain label for a bad moment, and a life can have several of them scattered anywhere. Nadir is stricter and grander: it names the one absolute bottom of the entire arc, the point below every other, in a register built for histories.

A trough is the dip between peaks on a chart, and the word itself expects recovery — another peak is assumed to follow. A nadir makes no such promise and admits no rival: it is the single deepest point the whole curve ever reaches.

Nadir is a loan from medieval Arabic astronomy, and it came alone: no prefix, no suffix, no English cousins built on its root. Its only companion is its sky-chart partner zenith — the highest point, a word you met earlier in this course — which arrived by the same route.
Nadir means the lowest point something reaches.

Morale on the expedition reached its nadir on day forty, when the stove failed, the sat phone died, and the two doctors stopped speaking to each other; everything after that, the leader wrote, felt like ascent.
Nadir marks the single bottom of a long arc — one point, not a stretch of general badness.
Astronomers coined it for the spot in the sky directly beneath your feet, the exact opposite of the zenith overhead, and the figurative use keeps that geometry: from the nadir, every direction is up.
Nadir dresses a low point in observatory robes — use it for the dramatic bottom of a career, a reputation, or an era, especially in writing that steps back and surveys the whole arc.
In conversation, rock bottom or low point carries the same news without the telescope.

The museum's timeline wall does not hide the year 1962.
Attendance had thinned for a decade, but that spring the roof failed, the insurer balked, and the whole Egyptian wing closed behind plywood.
A curator's diary from June records guards outnumbering visitors on four days out of five.
Historians of the institution agree in calling 1962 its nadir: in a century and a half of ledgers, no other year reached so far down.
The climb back took twenty years and a lottery grant — which is a different story, told farther along the wall.
